findings.detail: The recommendation says what to do but not why the clients want to do it: to simplify their investments. The historical valuation also adds transaction-level detail to a section the specification asks to keep high level.
report_quote: We recommend disinvesting the joint GIA in full. We recommend using the gross proceeds of c. £45,000 to top up David’s and Susan’s Stocks & Shares ISAs equally for the new tax year.
Your joint General Investment Account was previously shown in our records (15 March) as £40,000.

findings.detail: This presents putting all the estimated proceeds into the ISAs as the plan, although the meeting note says both ISAs are already part-funded and the top-ups use their remaining allowances. The following adviser marker acknowledges that the amounts and destination of any excess still need resolving.
report_quote: We recommend using the gross proceeds of c. £45,000 to top up David’s and Susan’s Stocks & Shares ISAs equally for the new tax year.

findings.detail: The report follows the ownership and meeting decisions without leaking internal guidance. It does not, however, date the approximate £45,000 live-meeting valuation, despite the instruction to consider the date of a figure before relying on it; the separate historical figure is dated.
report_quote: | H-GIA-J | David Clarke & Susan Clarke | General Investment Account | c. £45,000 |

findings.detail: The repeated opening is unnecessary, and ‘GIA’, ‘disinvesting’ and ‘CGT’ make the advice less plain than it could be. The meaning remains broadly understandable.

findings.detail: All four markers identify the charge, tax question or ISA allocation requiring confirmation and name the relevant account or platform.
